test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Consider the magnetic field produced by a current carrying solenoid. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The solenoid in a way acts similar to the bar magnet.
The magnetic field near the centre of long solenoid is nearly constant.
The magnitude of the magnetic field outside but close to the solenoid is extremely large.
The strength of the magnetic field increases if we increase the number of turns.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The magnitude of the magnetic field outside but close to the solenoid is extremely large**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Solenoid and its Magnetic Field:**

 
• A solenoid is a coil of wire wound into a tightly packed helix. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• When an electric current flows through the solenoid, it produces a magnetic field. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is nearly uniform and strong. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• This uniform field is one of the key characteristics of a solenoid. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field lines inside the solenoid are parallel to the axis of the solenoid. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field outside the solenoid is relatively weak and spreads out.
 
• The magnetic field lines form closed loops, entering the solenoid at one end and exiting at the other.
 
• The solenoid behaves similarly to a bar magnet, with distinct north and south poles. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The strength of the magnetic field inside the solenoid is directly proportional to the current flowing through it. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The strength of the magnetic field is also directly proportional to the number of turns of wire per unit length. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Increasing the number of turns increases the magnetic field strength. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field near the center of a long solenoid is nearly constant, meaning it has the same strength at different points along the axis. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field outside the solenoid, especially at a distance, diminishes rapidly.
 
• The magnetic field lines outside the solenoid form loops that close back to the solenoid.
 
• The magnetic field outside but close to the solenoid is not extremely large; it is relatively weak compared to the inside.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field drops off rapidly as you move away from the solenoid.
 
• The end faces of the solenoid act as magnetic poles. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Solenoids are used in many electrical components, such as relays and electromagnets. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The magnetic field inside of the solenoid is uniform, where as the field outside is non-uniform. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The direction of the magnetic field can be determined by the right-hand rule
